message:
I see. When an exception is raised during `OP_RETURN`, the `pc` is at the `OP_RETURN` instruction. But the `ci->pc` for the current frame was set when the `OP_RETURN` instruction was fetched, so `ci->pc` points to one past the `OP_RETURN` instruction. If `OP_RETURN` is the last instruction in the iseq, then `ci->pc` points to one past the end.

But wait - in the `L_RAISE` path, when the exception is raised, `ci` is the current frame. The `pc` is at the `OP_RETURN` instruction. Then `each_backtrace` is called with `pc = &mrb->c->cibase[i].pc[-1]`, which is `ci->pc - 1`. If `ci->pc` points to one past the end, then `pc` points to the last instruction, and `idx = pc - irep->iseq = irep->ilen - 1`, which is `< irep->ilen`. So that wouldn't trigger the bug.

Hmm, let me think about this differently. The issue might be with `OP_TAILCALL`. Let me look at how tail calls work:

<｜｜DSML｜｜>
<parameter=command>grep -n "OP_TAILCALL" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/mruby/src/vm.c | head -10</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
